key_insight: BoxMind introduces a precise, hierarchical representation of boxing actions (atomic punch events with temporal, spatial and technical attributes) and uses a closed-loop AI system to optimize and validate in elite competition at the 2024 Olympics.
problem_solved: Combat sports lack structured, interpretable spatiotemporal representations and closed-loop strategy systems that can turn raw match footage into actionable tactical insights for elite boxing.
method: Define atomic punch events with exact temporal boundaries plus spatial and technical attributes, and organize them into an 18-node hierarchical technical–tactical taxonomy.
Automatically parse match video into the hierarchical event stream (detection + attribute classification) to produce an interpretable tactical trace.
Use a closed-loop optimization pipeline that ingests parsed traces to recommend and evaluate strategy adjustments, validated on elite-level (2024 Olympics) competition data.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a reproducible blueprint for converting dense spatiotemporal sports footage into interpretable action primitives and applying closed-loop strategy optimization — enabling better model interpretability, tactical evaluation, and real-world validation.
visual_elements: Timeline diagram showing atomic punch events with start/end times and layered attributes (type, target, force/distance).
Hierarchical tree/flowchart of the 18 technical–tactical nodes to illustrate taxonomy and grouping.
System diagram of the closed-loop pipeline: video → event parsing → strategy optimizer → coach/athlete feedback → re-evaluation.
Heatmap or ring-chart overlay of spatial punch distributions and tactical outcomes across rounds (Olympic validation case).
paper_title: BoxMind: Closed-loop AI strategy optimization for elite boxing validated in the 2024 Olympics
paper_authors: Kaiwen Wang, Kaili Zheng, Rongrong Deng, Qingmin Fan, Milin Zhang
